what.text: Vitamin B6 is a vitamin. Pyridoxine is its plant form. The body turns it into pyridoxal phosphate, which helps enzymes break down protein, carbohydrate and fat.

src.label: Pyridoxine Hydrochloride Injection, USP label (Fresenius Kabi), DailyMed

research.text: We found no published human study of injected vitamin B6, alone or in lipotropic blends, for energy or fat loss.

us.text: Pyridoxine hydrochloride injection is FDA approved, as a generic (ANDA) product, for pyridoxine deficiency. Injecting it for energy or weight loss is off-label.
FDA’s Drugs@FDA data lists Fresenius Kabi’s pyridoxine hydrochloride injection, an ANDA with an original approval dated August 1972.

items.text: Pyridoxine deficiency from poor diet, from drugs such as isoniazid or oral contraceptives, or from inborn errors such as B6-dependent seizures. The injection is for when taking it by mouth is not possible or absorption is impaired.

items.text: “Single deficiency, as of pyridoxine alone, is rare.”

items.text: FDA lists pyridoxine hydrochloride as nominated for outsourcing-facility (503B) compounding and “under evaluation” (Category 1), marked as a component of an FDA-approved drug.

src.label: FDA, Bulk drug substances nominated under section 503B (categories)

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. That includes compounded lipotropic injection blends containing B6.

src.label: FDA, Compounding and the FDA: Q&A

us.text: FDA’s recall records list many compounded “lipotropic”, “Lipo-B” and methionine/inositol/choline (MIC) injections recalled by compounding pharmacies, most often for “lack of assurance of sterility.” Examples: Isomeric Pharmacy Solutions’ cyanocobalamin/methionine/inositol/choline vials (2017), Partell Specialty Pharmacy’s MIC + B12 vials (2018), Assurance Infusion’s Lipo B vials (2020) and Tailor Made Compounding’s MIC + B12 + carnitine vials (2022). These were recalls of specific pharmacies’ lots, not a ruling on the ingredients.

world.lead: Pyridoxine injection is an approved medicine for B6 deficiency in the US. EMA’s list of centrally authorised medicines has no pyridoxine product. Canada, the UK, national EU status and Australia were not confirmed.

countries.status: Approved medicine (pyridoxine hydrochloride injection, generic) for B6 deficiency. Prescription-only. Energy or weight-loss use is off-label.

after.text: Vitamin B6 is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Separately, the lists' method M2.2 bans intravenous infusions or injections of more than 100 mL per 12-hour period, except in hospital treatment, surgery or clinical tests.

side.text: The pyridoxine injection label lists tingling or numbness (paresthesia), sleepiness and low folic acid levels.

items.text: Paresthesia, somnolence, and low serum folic acid levels.

unconfirmed: We could not open the Drugs@FDA web pages; the approval date comes from FDA’s Drugs@FDA data through openFDA.
The FDA injection label lists paresthesia but does not use the term peripheral neuropathy; we could not reach TGA’s or other regulators’ records on B6 and nerve damage, so that is left out.
Canada, UK (MHRA), national EU and Australian (TGA) status could not be confirmed from the regulators’ records.
surprises: B6 is sold in lipotropic shots for energy and fat loss, but the FDA label approves the injection only for deficiency and says a deficiency of pyridoxine alone is rare.
